stem.en: Kabir says the alphonso mango "has been the same tree for two hundred years, so its DNA has not changed at all". What does the cutting sim say?

text.en: Every cutting adds a few slips, and two hundred years of cuttings have added many. The trees are near-identical, not identical, and the accumulated slips are why some orchards' alphonsos differ slightly from others'.

feedback.en: One in a billion per letter, per division, over centuries of divisions, is thousands of letters by now.

text.en: Completely different, like any two trees.

feedback.en: Thousands of letters out of hundreds of millions is still near-identical. That is why it still tastes like alphonso.

text.en: The DNA is renewed each year with the leaves.

feedback.en: New leaves are made by mitosis from the same tape, slips and all.

explanation.en: Clones drift apart slowly, by the slips in every copy. Slowly is not never.
